newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha prices little changed in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha prices little changed in quiet trade.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices were little changed on Thursday in a dull market almost devoid of participants, traders said.
Open-spec naphtha for first-half February, which is the most active trading period, was assessed at $227.00/229.00. It was sold to a Western trader at $228.50 on Wednesday.
Second-half January was nominally quoted at $231.00/234.00, compared with late Wednesday's $231.75/232.75.
In inter-month naphtha spreads, second-half January/second-half February was discussed at plus $6.00/8.00, and first-half February/first-half March at plus $5.00/5.50.

In physical naphtha trading, a Japanese petrochemical firm bought a spot cargo to be delivered to Chiba, east of Tokyo, in the second half of January. The price was believed to be around $6.00 over the mean of Japanese quotes.

In the middle distillates, offers for January delivery jet kerosene cargoes were notionally quoted at around $2.00 over the mean of Singapore quotes on a cost and freight (C and F) basis with tight regional supplies, while buyers were said to be aiming for the rollover of the December level, which is a premium of around $1.60, traders said.
